messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden rise in 502/504 + timeouts hitting prod-gateway (gw-prod-us). Error rate spiked ~08:12 UTC, 10m window. Triggered page to #incidents.

sarah: acked. I'm oncall. seeing 502s from gateway -> upstream nginx/proxy 504s. beginning triage. :eyes:

mike: looking at ingress metrics now. 5xx is concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/stream endpoints. ratio: ~12% 5xx on generate, 7% timeouts on stream. tail latency upstream shows a long tail > 15s.

nilesh: quick note — traces are sparse: sampling dropped recently in a rolling config change (we set global_sampler=0.02 yesterday). large portion of problematic requests have no spans. missing request-id header in many logs, so correlating is hard.

sarah: ugh. so we have both increased errors and blind spots in traces. start with mitigation to reduce customer impact.

mike: proposed immediate mitigations:
- route heavy customers to last-known-stable model variant (lower mem IO)
- increase gateway timeouts slightly to avoid premature 504s while we investigate
- revert the sampler change to 0.1 for prod as a stopgap

nilesh: on the sampling revert — that requires control-plane push; I can do a targeted rollout to gw-prod-us only. But we also need a stopgap logging shim to capture request-id/latency for untraced requests.

olivia: assigning myself for handoff in 10m. please capture all action items in thread for next on-call.

sarah: mike, can you open rollback for sampler? @deploy-bot can we roll control-plane sampler config to 0.1 for gw-prod-us? deploy-bot: started canary.

deploy-bot: control-plane-config: sampler=0.1 -> canary(10% gw-prod-us) at 08:18 UTC. monitor for config errors.

mike: also bumped gateway read_timeout to 28s from 20s in gw-prod-us to avoid cascading 504s. command run:
```bash
# increase timeout on gw-prod-us
rwctl gateway set-timeout --region us --timeout 28s
```

sarah: Cassie in support reported customer impact: two high-tier customers (AcmeApps, BrightQ) saw API failures during billing jobs and streaming timeouts. Cassie, any notes on customer severity? 
cassie-support: AcmeApps reported retries and delayed jobs (SLA risk). BrightQ has streaming interruptions but they can failover to dedicated for now. Raising P1 to account for potential SLA breach.

nilesh: stopgap logging shim for edge to capture missing request-ids and latencies. patch (Go, tiny middleware) we applied to a canary pod:
```go
// simple middleware to ensure request-id and log latency
func ReqLog(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
  return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    id := r.Header.Get("x-rw-reqid")
    if id == "" { id = uuid.New().String(); }
    start := time.Now()
    w.Header().Set("x-rw-reqid", id)
    next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
    log.Printf("req=%s method=%s path=%s dur_ms=%d status=%d", id, r.Method, r.URL.Path, time.Since(start).Milliseconds(), getStatus(w))
  })
}
```

mike: good. that will at least give us structured logs to stitch partial traces. rolling that to 20% of pods in gw-prod-us now.

sarah: running log collector queries. example grep to find newly instrumented logs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app=gateway,canary=true -n prod | grep "req=" | tail -n 200
```

nilesh: note — we still have a missing-span situation for requests that hit our cached KV layer and short-circuit; those were excluded from tracing by an older filter. I'm pushing a small patch to include kv.fastpath spans for tracing and to attach request-id header when short-circuiting.

mike: we observed KV cache evictions coincident with latency spikes — eviction storm led to extra backend calls. adding a short-term throttle on cache refreshes to reduce load. Command to change throttle:
```bash
rwctl cache set-refresh-throttle --policy gradual --rate 100/s --scope gw-prod-us
```

sarah: Customer impact summary (for incident doc): ~8-12% of requests to /v1/generate experienced 5xx or timeouts in the 08:12-08:40 window. Impacted customers: AcmeApps (retries causing delayed pipelines), BrightQ (stream dropouts), and a handful of smaller customers with long-running streaming sessions.

cassie-support: notifying top 10 customers proactively with templated message. linking to status page.

olivia: taking handoff at 08:25 UTC. Handoff notes:
- mitigations applied: sampler canary -> increasing sampling to 0.1; gateway timeout increased; request-id middleware rolled to canary; cache throttle applied.
- next: monitor 5xx% and trace volume for the next 30m; if 5xx > 3% for more than 10m -> escalate to infra.
- action owner mapping: nilesh -> tracing/revert rules; mike -> cache throttle & upstream scaling; cassie -> customer comms; sarah -> incident doc + postmortem starter.

sarah: quick check on rollout health: sampler canary shows trace volume up 4x in canary pods, no errors. middleware logs present. 5xx dropped from 12% -> 4% in 10m after throttle and timeout bump.

mike: can we keep the canary middleware at 20% for 30m then promote? prefer to wait until trace coverage confirms correlation.

olivia: agreed. I'll keep 20% for now and take over monitoring. setting reminder for 08:55 UTC to reevaluate and either promote or rollback. also file a follow-up to remove the temporary read_timeout increase once stable.

pagerduty-bot: Incident ongoing. P1 assigned to oncall(s): sarah -> olivia (handoff). Next update due in 30m.

sarah: logging note for postmortem: root causes we suspect: 1) sampler change reduced trace coverage and slowed triage 2) cache eviction storm increased backend load -> long tail latencies -> 504s 3) missing request-id propagation made correlation harder. Temporary fixes: sampler revert, middleware, cache throttle, timeout bump.

mike: will prepare a perf regression test for cache refresh path and evaluate kvcache eviction thresholds.

nilesh: follow-ups: push a permanent change to ensure request-id is injected at the edge for all short-circuited flows; increase default trace sampling to 0.05 and make config gated by a rollout MRC.

olivia: thanks team. I'm taking the pager. will update in thread or call if things regress. :hand:

cassie-support: drafting customer message now; will share before sending.

sarah: closing active mitigation steps in this thread; tagging for postmortem and scheduling a 1-hour RCA tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
